entries.title: My restless dreams reveal myself to me, and nonconsensually too
entries.entry: I didn't write shit all summer. I didn't finish this damn journal. I left a lot of things incomplete because I wanted to learn new things and just didn't feel like using AI for the sake of "getting shit done". But here we are. I'm back at it finishing this journal and starting to build other widgets and sites for a series of workshop on digital literature and archives. Good enough. Okay. Recently, I haven't been sleeping well. I've always had sleeping issues, but I've gotten better over my lifetime, so when sleep *does* get bad these days, I actually notice it. But I'm coming out of that bout. Nightmares subsiding, details less vivid and less oft written to memory. But last night was hard enough. Last night, I slept early. I was tired sooner than expected, at 10 pm, so I slept. I dreamed of many things I don't remember, luckily. But, I do remember Justin. We were at what felt to be some sort of reuinion. We got time to ourselves. It was the same as it used to be. Just as I leaned into him for a kiss, I woke up. Holding his hand only in my head, but I could still feel it there. Leaning on him, until I realized it was my bed  I pressed against. Terribly sad and disappiointed by the reality that we'll never have had our moment. Just always missing our opportunity, passing over each other once the other was ready. And so much of life moves thus; my despair deepens. I miss my youthful sense of love. I miss the feeling of hope that there is potential for a perfect match. That sense of hope that's limitless and eternal. I miss feeling loved. seen, belonging. But the reality is that I don't feel love like I used to, and the hope and love I've felt for so many are just unrequitted feelings. So many ends that are incomprehensible to me. Despair, because if I understood it, I could fix it. Despair because I realize that thought is as much an illusion as my juvenile naitivite. Life is not graspable. Growing up is learning that. It's why it feels so lonely. This realization brings a dread that's too heavy a weight for how frequently it occurs. So, at some poiint, I stop hoping and settle for indifference. No, I pray to settle for indifference, because then I'd have respite from the harder feelings. At least indifference is surviviable. I find myself often hoping for indifference, savoring when I finally have room to breathe. Recently, that indiffernce has been lasting, I feel lucky that I can be functional day to day. But processing the pain when it bubbles up does also bring peace and clarity... And I guess deep down I  still have hopes of being able to feel that kind of love again someday.
showerthoughts: Well, I finished the lil bit I was stuck on for this journal -- automating list rendering. Now I get to add a footer and minimization widget

I'm so pessimistic in my journal writing LMAO. I SWEAR IM MORE PEPPY IN PERSON (she is in fact not more peppy in person. The dark corners of the planet and the mind are one of her special interest rip)

I'm so happy to have gotten to be conscious during the early 2000s and a 2010s emo teen. Like what a fucking time. I just wish I got to experience being a 20something gen x-er going to raves when it was about losing your shit and cutting lose, not peacocking not even to impress those around you but  racking up stacks of likes and views... x-ers and millenials looked like they were having SO much fun finding ways to bend rules and make shit up...
I did get that mp3 player to work btw. Plus textile speakers and the electronic part of my plant monitor. I think after this workshop is done I'll make a personal site to share my projects

entries.title: I be im Berlin, camp at DWeb Camp
entries.entry: Visited my friend in Berlin and was enlightedned by the kind of art that the state supports financially. Interactive theater especially, for its technical possibilitys and depth of immersion in a story. It's also been fun becoming closer friends with people now that we're outside of a professional setting. At DWeb camp, apathetic about technical futures, but reluctantly inspired by people representing communities that have done well so far.

entries.title: Catching up, having fun, working hard
entries.entry: It's sunday, I'm sitting in a coffee shop called Nook in Bushwick. After a stormy night and a relatively poor decision to hang out with a friend rather than go to a tech event for creative code relevant to my research interests, the sun is shining, I'm taking time to read and learn and to make improvements to this journal. I promised myself this summer that I would take advantage of my time at the Recurse Center and, as they say, work at the edge of my abilities-- push myself to increase my skillset. Next week is 4/12, a third through my cohort, and I'm just now getting to the push. Better one-third than never. I have been working with electronics. I built an mp3 player (not yet successful), and a textile speaker at some workshops with NYC Resistor. This week, I will read and study, and work with a fellow Recursor on a project I came up with: a plant monitor. It will take in visual and environmental sensor data and tell the user ... things about their plant. Ultimately I'd like to tie this into a prospective project with the Palestine Seed Library to make smart growing accessible. We'll see. Anyway, I'm also having fun. I started ballet finally, to learn dance techniques I can transfer to contact staff and am also doing some aerial things. Cannot complain. Except of course for inflation, growing wage gaps, tech fears and woes, etc.
showerthoughts: Just trust your gut with people. Yes, they're complicated and have their reasons, but in regards to how they relate to and are/n't compatible with you, it's their behavior that counts.

People struggle to accept and make room for experiences and perspectives misaligning with their own. I'm not sure if this is due as much to the protective quality of the ego as much as how people project that protective need, creating a culture in which seeing things differently is a hostility.

entries.title: A week gone by in vain?
entries.entry: And thus is the conclusion of my first trip to Bogota, Colombia, anywwhere south of the U.S. border, and the nearest I've been to the equator. Can I say that much is learned? Leaps and boudns in knowledge and connection? My analogue journal yet again empty. My travels limited by my own fears. I stuck largely to places I know at the advice of locals who also confine themselves to few parts of the city. But with a dear college friend who, admittedly not well, I felt I could move more as they do. Although their free movementh has not come without troubles (they explained a few sketchy encounters and muggings), generally they have no worries moving about. Similar to New York or really any major city, as long as you don't leave yourself exposed or vulnerable, it's hard to be an obvious target, and so you're left to chance. In fact, the most disconcerting events couldn't even be labeld as such; vagabounds selling candy, homeless exclaim in despair or ask politely for pocket change, most notably, a clown with tricks and dulces for sale. This is far less alarming than the physical assaults increasingly common in the cesspool called the greatest city on Earth: New York, New York. A place I call my home. I will arrive past midnight just in time for the unnerving period between 12 - 5 am and will opt for an uber (also a increasingly discomforting experience) in hopes of avoiding more spit in my face by a wreaking, mumbling, spiteful poor soul. While the vice of Bogota may be stealing, their virtue is kindness and grace, and at least there's a reason for that harm. What excuse do we have for failing those unwell and leaving them on the streat to actualize to the populus the peril they've been forced to carry within?

entries.title: A flight to Bogota, and all around me: Hell.
entries.entry: I am exhausted all the time. More than I have ever been in life. Thinking back on my analogue journal, all i can feel is envy for a younger self. I used to sit in cafes and draw what I saw, take pictures of what I learned and reflect. But now, I am just too tired to be mindful of my surroundings it seems. It feels like I've lost the point, and with it the desire. It is not an envy of lost youth --if 30 is an end to that, life as a human is doomed. It's that there seemed to be more to hope for. More hope in individuals, that they would turn to good, within themselves and thus collectively towards a better tomorrow. That a better tomorrow was the inevitanle outcome of that labor. But as I sit on this plane, a sea of clouds in a cirrus soup below, an inexplicably beautfiful bending of light from dune orange to darkened teal, a red sun, I can only think of those who cannot fly away. The US and Israel declared war on Iran just days ago, its declaration being bombs that bring civilian perish. In the name of liberation of the Iranian people, claims Trump. And of course Iran responded by attacking neighboring nations hosting American bases. So far the retaliation is contained to those bases, though shrapnel has fallen on civilians elsewhere. We've lost 6 service members, but this pales to the >1000 painfully pointless civilian deaths in Iran. Saudi, the UAE, Levanon, Jordan, and a few other nations are all in the crossfire. Hezbollah's involvement has caused division not only in Lebanon but also within themselves. We are all so fucking done with the unnecessary political moves that do not help the majority of us on Earth. Even I, while on an all-expenses paid trip to an academic conference in Bogota, with a stable salary enough for savings, a loving partner and friends, hobbies, health, and a job that I enjoy thoroughly -- am losing the point. I can only imagine how my cousins, who escaped war in Sudan just to end up back in the belly of the beast, my Palestinian friend who has had her home ripped from her house by house to be burnt and paved by those whose ancestors knew no shortage of loss, and now take relentlessly, just to be on watch in Jordan. Anyway, I finally got around to watching Wicked, the Wizard of Oz woke retelling in the 2014s fashion whose social commentary's so on the nose it makes me cringe, but reminiscient of the hope we had back then. Except it came out in the mid 2020s, and the cast seems to have reverted to the heroin sheek period. I think I've fully accepted that where we live is in Hell.
